fact_text: A foreign professional hired for specialized or technical work must be paid at least the national average monthly salary set by the Ministry of Labor, currently NTD 47,971 per month. A salary offer below that floor cannot support a work permit, whatever the role.
evidence_quote: foreigners employed in specialized and technical works whose monthly salary shall not be lower than the average monthly salary published by the central competent authority.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any job offer qualifies for a work permit. Actually there is a hard monthly-salary floor tied to the national average (NTD 47,971); an offer below it is rejected. Action: confirm the gross monthly salary clears the current threshold before signing.

entity_title: Your employer files the work permit, not you
fact_text: For a standard foreign-professional job, the Taiwan employer, not the employee, files the work-permit application with the Workforce Development Agency (Ministry of Labor) through the EZ Work Permit platform. The Ministry of Labor approval must exist before the employee applies for the residence visa and ARC.
evidence_quote: According to Article 7 of Regulations on the Permission and Administration of the Employment of Foreign Workers, employers hiring foreigners shall apply online via the EZ Work Permit platform

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you apply for your own Taiwan work visa. Actually the employer holds and files the work permit with the Ministry of Labor; you cannot self-apply on the standard route (only the Employment Gold Card is self-sponsored). Action: have the employer start the EZ Work Permit filing before planning travel.

entity_title: Self-sponsor with the Employment Gold Card
fact_text: The Taiwan Employment Gold Card bundles an open work permit, residence permit and visa into one document that the professional applies for directly, with no employer sponsor or prior job offer needed. Because the work permit is open, the holder can work for or switch to any employer.
evidence_quote: The Taiwan Employment Gold Card is a combined open work permit, residence permit and visa for skilled professionals.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every Taiwan work route needs an employer sponsor tied to one job. Actually the Gold Card is self-sponsored and its work permit is open, so it survives an employer change. Action: if you qualify in one of the eligible fields, weigh the Gold Card against an employer-tied permit.

entity_title: Apply for the ARC within 30 days of entry
fact_text: A foreign national who enters Taiwan on a residence visa must apply for the Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) within 30 days, counted from the day after entry. Missing the window is finable, and the count starts the day after arrival, not on the arrival day itself.
evidence_quote: Foreign nationals entering the State with a residence visa must apply for an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) within thirty (30) days from the day following their entry into the State.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Many third-party guides say you have 15 days. The current NIA guideline gives 30 days, counted from the day following entry, and fines a missed deadline. Action: book the NIA appointment in your first weeks and do not count the arrival day.

entity_title: Report a move or job change to NIA in 30 days
fact_text: During residence, an ARC holder who changes home address or place of employment must register the change with the National Immigration Agency within 30 days of the event. Failure to do so is finable.
evidence_quote: In the event that a foreign national changes his/her resident address or his/her place of employment during the period of his/her residence, he/she shall apply to the NIA for registering the change within thirty (30) days, calculating from the next day of the occurrence of the event.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the ARC address is fixed at issuance. Actually every change of residential address or employer must be re-registered with NIA within 30 days or you are fined. Action: notify NIA whenever you move apartments or change jobs.

fact_text: To sponsor dependents onto ARCs as a foreign technical-professional worker, the sponsor must show average monthly total income of at least NTD 53,000 over the past year. Applicants who still hold a residence visa are exempt, so the income test mainly bites at extension or change of status.
evidence_quote: average monthly total income of at least NTD 53,000 for the past year is required (applicants holding residence visas are exempt from this requirement).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work permit alone lets you bring family. Actually sponsoring dependents as a technical professional requires proving at least NTD 53,000 average monthly income for the prior year (waived while you still hold a residence visa). Action: keep income evidence for the dependent ARC application, especially at renewal.

entity_title: Employees join NHI from day one, not after 6 months
fact_text: The general rule is that ARC holders join National Health Insurance only after 6 months of residence, but foreign nationals employed with a work permit are enrolled by their employer starting the first day of employment. Expect NHI premium deductions from your first payroll.
evidence_quote: But those people who get work permits with ARC must join the National Health Insurance program by their employer starting the day they are employed.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed all newcomers wait 6 months for NHI. Actually the 6-month wait applies to the unemployed and dependents; employed ARC holders are enrolled by the employer from day one of employment. Action: budget for NHI payroll deductions immediately and use the coverage from your start date.

entity_title: Taxed at flat 18% until you reach 183 days
fact_text: Until a foreign employee has been present in Taiwan for 183 days in a calendar year, they are a non-resident taxpayer and salary is withheld at a flat 18%, well above resident progressive rates. Arriving late in the year means the first months are taxed at 18% before residency is reached.
evidence_quote: The withholding tax rate on salaries is 18%.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you immediately pay Taiwan's low resident tax rates. Actually, before you accumulate 183 days in a calendar year you are a non-resident taxed at a flat 18% on salary. Action: if you arrive in the second half of the year, plan cashflow for 18% withholding and reconcile once you cross 183 days.

entity_title: APRC needs 5 years at 183+ days each
fact_text: A foreign professional can apply for permanent residence (APRC) after five consecutive years of legal residence in Taiwan with an average annual residence of 183 days or more. Long absences that drop a year below 183 days can break the qualifying clock.
evidence_quote: Foreign professionals who engage in professional work in the State and have legally resided in the State for five (5) consecutive years with an average annual residence of 183 days or more

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any five years in Taiwan yields permanent residence. Actually each of the five consecutive years generally needs 183+ days of presence; heavy travel can reset eligibility. Action: track days in Taiwan each year if APRC is the goal.

entity_title: Top earners can reach APRC in one year
fact_text: Foreign specialist professionals get a faster APRC path: three years of continuous residence at 183+ days per year, or just one year (183+ days) if their Taiwan salary plus professional-practice income for the most recent year totals at least NTD 6,000,000.
evidence_quote: Having legally resided in the State for one (1) year, residing more than 183 days, and having domestic salary income and professional practice income in the most recent year totaling at least NTD 6,000,000.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed permanent residence always takes five years. Actually a foreign specialist professional can qualify in three years, or in a single year if they earn at least NTD 6,000,000 that year. Action: high earners recognised as specialist professionals should check the accelerated APRC route.

entity_title: You now get a 6% labor pension, no APRC needed
fact_text: Since 1 January 2026, foreign professionals and specialist professionals doing professional work in Taiwan are covered by the new labor pension system regardless of permanent-residency status; the employer must contribute at least 6% of monthly wages to a Bureau of Labor Insurance pension account. Before 2026 this applied only to those with permanent residence.
evidence_quote: they shall be covered by the new labor pension system regardless of whether they have obtained permanent residency status.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed foreign employees get no Taiwan pension unless they hold an APRC (true before 2026). Actually, from 1 January 2026 all foreign professionals in professional work are in the new labor pension system with a 6%-of-wages employer contribution, regardless of permanent residency. Action: confirm the employer opens your BLI pension account; you may keep the old system only by written notice before 30 June 2026.

entity_title: Halve tax on salary above NTD 3 million
fact_text: A qualifying foreign special professional (including many Gold Card holders) may exclude from taxable income half of the annual salary that exceeds NTD 3,000,000, in each of up to five tax years in which they reside in Taiwan for 183+ days. Certain overseas income is also excluded from the basic-income (AMT) calculation.
evidence_quote: half of the amount of the salary income exceeding the NT$3,000,000 of each such taxable year in which he/she resides in the R.O.C. for 183 days or more may be excluded from the gross income for the assessment of individual income tax liability.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed all Taiwan salary is fully taxed. Actually a qualifying foreign special professional can exclude half of salary above NTD 3,000,000 for five years, plus certain overseas income from the AMT base. Action: confirm foreign-special-professional status and file the income-tax exemption application.
